title: Choose the look for Dictate Studio
question: Comps generated with ChatGPT Images. The roll assigned Edit Controller. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Edit Controller
options.lineage: Sony BVE edit controllers and CMX 3600 edit decision lists
options.thesis: Every review is an edit decision list: numbered events, timecodes, and the words that go with them.
options.viewport: Program monitor owns the left; the EDL runs down the right as numbered events; a key row (MARK IN · MARK OUT · PIN · BOX · TALK) sits under the picture with a big timecode readout.
options.risk: Tips into retro cosplay if keycaps and segment digits are overdone; Arabic transcripts need a proportional face inside the EDL.

raised.raise: Nothing disappears, it cancels: deleted notes strike through as VOID and can be restored until you submit.
Nothing is labeled twice: every control says its job once, in one place.
Rank comes from weight, case, and reversal, not a ladder of type sizes.
Timecode digits sit on the whole-pixel grid, never blurred by scaling.
Every frame grab shows at one fixed scale and ground, so notes compare at a glance.

options.label: Broadcast Gallery
options.lineage: TV production gallery: monitor wall, under-monitor displays, tally lights, talkback
options.thesis: You are the director in the gallery: talk, point at a monitor, and the crew takes the note.
options.viewport: A monitor wall: your picture large, pages or frames as smaller monitors each with a label strip; a red tally rim lights whichever monitor you are talking about.
options.risk: Closest to the dark-UI-with-red-accent look many recording tools ship; familiarity is its cost.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.lineage: darkroom printer's exposure record over a zone-system ramp
options.thesis: A neutral eleven-step gray ramp as the only tones, so your eye judges footage, not the interface.
options.viewport: Translucent note sheets slide over the frame; marked regions take hatch density, one magenta reserved for corrections.
options.case: Fuses well for a colorist's eye; loses on clarity because hatching on a frame competes with your own pins and boxes.
options.risk: Hatch overlays on top of video fight the marks you draw.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: 1960s airline ticket wallets and carbon coupons
options.thesis: Each note a coupon that stamps itself validated, used, or void.
options.viewport: A coupon book of notes, one leg per sheet.
options.case: Fuses poorly: creators don't think in travel coupons.
options.risk: Charming, but the metaphor hides the video.

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every session a catalog number on matte black.
options.viewport: A stacked waveform plot of the session owns the field.
options.case: Fuses poorly: color-coded labels hurt a task tool's clarity.
options.risk: Coded labels slow you down mid-review.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: pocket airline timetables on a light table
options.thesis: One type size; rank carried by weight and reversal.
options.viewport: Notes as raked slides along one axis.
options.case: Fuses poorly: raked containers fight a video frame.
options.kept: Rank by weight, case, and reversal.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: Low resolution worn proudly at poster scale.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no tie to video or web review.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.lineage: botanical plates following one plant through a season
options.thesis: Plates at one exact scale so change reads directly.
options.case: Fuses poorly: cream editorial world, wrong room.
options.risk: Soft and bookish for a production tool.
options.kept: Fixed scale and ground for every frame grab.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean, dark Frame.io-style review app, executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Video left, comment list right, purple primary buttons.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other review tool by design.
